collections.description: An event recorded in a ProcessInstance's lifecycle.

A human being. Stable identity whose relationships with the enterprise are expressed through Roles. A single Person entity persists across all engagements (hire, leave, return, convert to consultant) — entity_id never changes.

A time-bound engagement. Role is concrete (not abstract) because some generic engagements may be captured directly as Role instances. However, in practice most Roles are Domain-layer specializations. Exactly one of held_by_person or held_by_organization must be populated (enforced by the applications that write the data). Engagements that could be held by either (like VendorRole) carry both, with one populated.

buckets.name: CoreProcess
buckets.description: The core process model: definitions, steps and transitions (what a process is), and instances, step completions and events (each run of it). Workflow state lives here, never on Domain entities. Process definitions are data, created by applications; there is no business-specific process in the EDM.

properties.name: Foundation
properties.description: The permanent enterprise concepts. Entity is the root; Person, Organization (LegalEntity, OrganizationalUnit), Team, Role, Activity, Agreement, Asset, Address, Document and Period specialise it. Every Domain, Process and Application entity specialises exactly one of these kinds and carries its attributes (D12). Entity and Organization are never tables (edmAbstract).

properties.name: natural_identifiers
properties.description: Zero or more natural (business) keys that identify this entity. Each carries its own scheme and issuer so multiple identifier systems can coexist without conflict.

properties.name: value
properties.description: The identifier value itself.

properties.name: scheme
properties.description: The naming/numbering scheme. Examples: "employee_number", "tax_id", "iso_country_code", "ein", "ssn".

properties.name: issuer
properties.description: The authority that issued this identifier. Examples: "Acme HR", "IRS", "ISO", "National Social Security Administration".

properties.name: issued_at
properties.description: When the identifier was issued (if known).

properties.name: valid_from
properties.description: When this identifier becomes effective.

properties.name: valid_to

properties.description: Timestamp when this entity record was created.

properties.name: created_by
properties.description: Actor who created this entity record. May be a user identifier, system identifier, or service account name.

properties.name: last_modified_at
properties.description: Timestamp of last modification to this entity record.

properties.name: last_modified_by
properties.description: Actor who last modified this entity record.

properties.name: lifecycle_state
properties.description: Current lifecycle state of the entity. Each entity has its own list of states, held on this attribute with the meaning of each value (D3).
properties.valueDefinitions:
PROSPECT: Known to the enterprise but no formal engagement yet.
ACTIVE: Has at least one active Role with the enterprise.
INACTIVE: No currently-active Role but record remains.
MERGED: Record has been merged into another Person record.
ARCHIVED: Record is archived per data-retention policy.
DECEASED: Person is deceased; record retained for historical reference.

properties.name: state_effective_from
properties.description: When the current lifecycle state became effective.

properties.name: state_effective_to
properties.description: When the current lifecycle state ceases to be effective (if known).

properties.name: state_history
properties.description: Immutable history of lifecycle state transitions. Appended to on every state change; never mutated in place.

properties.name: from_state
properties.description: The prior lifecycle state (as enum string value).

properties.name: to_state
properties.description: The new lifecycle state (as enum string value).

properties.name: transition_timestamp
properties.description: When the transition occurred.

properties.name: transitioned_by_entity_type
properties.description: Entity type of transitioned by: one of Person, Role, Team. Polymorphic reference: no relationship (docs/patterns/polymorphic_references.md).

properties.name: transitioned_by_entity_id
properties.description: The actor responsible for the transition. Typically references a Person (via their entity_id), but may be a system/service account in automated transitions.

properties.name: reason
properties.description: Free-text reason or note explaining the transition.

properties.name: addresses
properties.description: Zero or more Address references. An entity may have multiple addresses (e.g., a customer with distinct billing and shipping addresses; a Person with home and work addresses).

A human being. Stable identity whose relationships with the enterprise are expressed through Roles. A single Person entity persists across all engagements (hire, leave, return, convert to consultant) — entity_id never changes.

properties.name: entity_id
properties.description: The globally unique, system-generated surrogate identifier. Never changes over the lifetime of the entity. This is the stable join key used across every system, report, and integration that references this entity. Business keys (employee number, invoice number) may change; entity_id does not.

properties.name: role_type
properties.description: The kind of role. Each Domain specialization binds to a specific value (e.g., EmployeeRole → EMPLOYEE).
properties.valueDefinitions:
EMPLOYEE: A Person engaged as a paid employee.
CONTRACTOR: A Person engaged under a contracting arrangement.
VENDOR: A Person or Organization engaged as a supplier.
VISITOR: A Person granted time-bound access to a facility.
CUSTOMER_CONTACT: A Person acting as contact at a customer Organization.
BOARD_MEMBER: A Person serving on a governing board.
COMMITTEE_CHAIR: A Person leading a committee.
COMMITTEE_MEMBER: A Person serving on a committee.
ADVISOR: A Person providing advisory services.
MANAGER: A Person with management authority over others.
ALUMNI: A former employee after separation.
PARTNER: A Person or Organization acting as a strategic partner.
CANDIDATE: A Person engaged as a job seeker (Talent Acquisition).
INTERVIEWER: A Person assigned to interview candidates (Talent Acquisition).

properties.name: held_by_person
properties.description: The Person who holds this role. Populated when the role is held by a human (employment, visit, board membership).

properties.name: held_by_organization_entity_type
properties.description: Entity type of held by organization: one of LegalEntity, OrganizationalUnit. Polymorphic reference: no relationship (docs/patterns/polymorphic_references.md).

properties.name: held_by_organization_entity_id
properties.description: The Organization holding this role. Populated when the role is held by an organization (e.g., a corporate vendor role, partner organization role).

properties.name: engaging_party_entity_type
properties.description: Entity type of engaging party: one of Person, Organization, LegalEntity, OrganizationalUnit, Team. Polymorphic reference: no relationship (docs/patterns/polymorphic_references.md).

properties.name: engaging_party_entity_id
properties.description: The party on the other side of the engagement — typically the Organization (or Team) that the holder is engaged with.

properties.name: role_title
properties.description: Human-readable title (e.g., "Senior Engineer", "Chair").

properties.name: effective_from
properties.description: Start of the role engagement.

properties.name: effective_to
properties.description: End of the role engagement (null if ongoing).

properties.name: end_reason
properties.description: Reason the role ended (resignation, separation, end-of-contract).

properties.name: authority_level
properties.description: Optional authority/seniority indicator (e.g., "signatory", "approver", "contributor"). Specialization classes may narrow this to controlled values.

A time-bound engagement. Role is concrete (not abstract) because some generic engagements may be captured directly as Role instances. However, in practice most Roles are Domain-layer specializations. Exactly one of held_by_person or held_by_organization must be populated (enforced by the applications that write the data). Engagements that could be held by either (like VendorRole) carry both, with one populated.

description: The core process model: definitions, steps and transitions (what a process is), and instances, step completions and events (each run of it). Workflow state lives here, never on Domain entities. Process definitions are data, created by applications; there is no business-specific process in the EDM.
